questions.q: What cabinet to use in the unit that is cost-efficient and sturdy/long-term?
questions.n: Aluminum is highly resistant to moisture, termites, and wear, making it a more durable and cost-effective long-term solution compared to wood-based panels in humid climates.

questions.q: What bedroom door is most suitable for a socialized condominium unit?
questions.n: Hollow core doors are lightweight and the most economical choice for interior applications where heavy-duty security is not required.

questions.q: Where should a water tank be properly located on a sloping site?
o: In a basement vault underneath the building.
Exactly in the middle of the slope.
questions.n: Placing the tank at the highest point utilizes gravity to distribute water to lower areas, reducing the need for constant pumping.

questions.q: What is the minimum floor area for a socialized condominium unit according to BP 220?
questions.n: BP 220 specifies 18 sqm as the minimum floor area for socialized housing units to ensure basic habitability. Note: the 2008 BP 220 IRR lists 18 m², but DHSUD–DEPDev price-ceiling rules now set larger minimums for a unit to qualify as socialized (24 m² for house-and-lot under JMC 2025-001).

questions.q: For a socialized condominium, what is the maximum number of storeys allowed before an elevator is strictly required?
questions.n: Under BP 220 standards for multi-family dwellings, an elevator is required for buildings beyond 6 storeys.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width for a main door in a socialized housing unit?
questions.n: The minimum clear width for the primary entrance door in BP 220 socialized housing is 0.80m.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width for bathroom and service doors?
questions.n: Secondary doors like those for bathrooms and service areas are permitted to have a smaller width of 0.70m.

questions.q: In socialized housing, what is the minimum ceiling height for a room with natural ventilation?
questions.n: For rooms relying on natural ventilation, the NBC/BP 220 requires a higher ceiling of 2.70m to allow for better air circulation.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a corridor in a multi-family dwelling or condominium?
questions.n: Corridors serving multiple units must have a minimum width of 1.20m to accommodate two-way pedestrian traffic.

questions.q: What is the minimum area for a single-occupancy bedroom?
questions.n: The minimum area for a bedroom is 6.00 sqm, with a least dimension of 2.00 meters.

questions.q: What is the most cost-effective flooring material for the common hallways of a socialized condo?
o: Unglazed Ceramic Tiles or Vinyl Tiles.
questions.n: These materials offer the best balance of low material cost, ease of installation, and durability for high-traffic areas.

questions.q: What type of paint is best for exterior concrete walls to resist tropical weather?
questions.n: Acrylic latex is water-based, flexible, and resistant to the high UV exposure and heavy rains characteristic of tropical climates.

questions.q: What board material is best for kitchen under-sink cabinets to prevent water damage?
questions.n: Marine plywood uses waterproof glue (WBP), making it capable of withstanding the frequent moisture exposure found under sinks.

questions.q: What is the standard size of a Concrete Hollow Block (CHB) used for exterior walls?
questions.n: The 6-inch (150mm) thickness is the standard for exterior load-bearing and non-load-bearing walls for better insulation and strength.

questions.q: What material is used for the "pantile" or roofing of socialized housing to ensure durability?
questions.n: Long-span G.I. (Galvanized Iron) sheets provide a continuous, durable, and leak-resistant roofing solution that is cost-effective for socialized housing.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Junction Box" in the electrical system of a unit?
o: To measure the amount of power used.
To house wire connections and protect them from the environment.
To act as a primary circuit breaker.
To increase the voltage of the electricity.
questions.n: Junction boxes provide a safe enclosure where electrical circuits branch off, ensuring connections are contained and accessible.

questions.q: In a high-rise condominium, what is the function of a "Transfer Pump"?
o: To move water from the ground cistern to the overhead water tank.
To drain water from the swimming pool.
To increase the water pressure in the faucets.
To filter the water from the main line.
questions.n: Transfer pumps overcome vertical distance to ensure the overhead tank remains full for gravity distribution.

questions.q: What color is used to identify fire protection pipes (sprinklers/standpipes)?
questions.n: In plumbing and fire safety codes, red is the universal color-coding for all fire-extinguishing system pipes.

questions.q: What is the function of a "Check Valve" in the plumbing system?
o: To prevent the backflow of water in the pipes.
To shut off the water during repairs.
To reduce the water pressure in the system.
To regulate the temperature of the water.
questions.n: A check valve is a one-way valve that allows fluid to flow in only one direction, protecting pumps and preventing contamination.

questions.q: What is the standard spacing for lighting outlets in a typical studio unit hallway?
questions.n: Spacing lighting at 3-meter intervals (roughly 10 feet) provides adequate, uniform illumination for safety in narrow hallways.

questions.q: What is the maximum travel distance to an exit in a building without sprinklers?
questions.n: The Fire Code of the Philippines mandates a maximum of 45m travel distance when no automatic fire suppression system is present.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a fire escape stair?
questions.n: For occupancy loads of 50 or more, the Fire Code specifies 1.12m as the minimum width for exit stairs.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Fire Curtain" in a basement parking area?
o: To provide shade for the parking attendants.
To contain smoke and fire within a specific zone.
To protect the floor from oil spills.
To hide the cars from the street.
questions.n: Fire curtains automatically deploy to create a barrier, preventing the spread of toxic smoke and heat across large open areas.

questions.q: What is the minimum fire-resistive rating for the walls between two separate condominium units?
o: No rating is required for socialized housing.
questions.n: The Building Code requires at least a 1-hour rating for party walls to prevent fire from spreading between adjacent units.

questions.q: What does "NFPA" stand for in relation to fire safety standards?
questions.n: The NFPA is the global authority that develops the codes and standards followed by most countries, including the Philippines.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of an elevator door per BP 344?
questions.n: BP 344 (Accessibility Law) requires 0.80m as the minimum clear opening to allow wheelchairs to enter and exit safely.

questions.q: How many PWD-accessible parking slots are required for a building with 25 parking slots?
questions.n: Accessibility standards generally require 1 PWD slot for the first 25 parking spaces provided.

questions.q: What is the required height of a handrail for a PWD ramp?
questions.n: BP 344 requires two levels of handrails: one at 0.70m for children or wheelchair users, and another at 0.90m for adults.

questions.q: What is the maximum slope of a ramp according to BP 344?
questions.n: The 1:12 ratio is the standard limit to ensure that wheelchair users can navigate the ramp without excessive physical strain.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimension of an elevator car for PWD access?
questions.n: This dimension allows a standard wheelchair to enter, turn, and have enough space for an attendant.

questions.q: What is the purpose of "Stirrups" in a concrete beam?
o: To make the concrete set faster.
questions.n: Stirrups are loops of rebar that wrap around the longitudinal bars to hold them together and resist diagonal tension (shear).

questions.q: What is the difference between a "Column" and a "Pier"?
o: There is no difference; the terms are used interchangeably.
A column is made of steel; a pier is always made of stone.
A column is horizontal; a pier is vertical.
A column is a vertical structural member; a pier is a short, thick column or foundation member.
questions.n: Columns are typically slender and part of the main frame, while piers are stockier and often used in foundations or bridges.

questions.q: What is the standard concrete mix ratio for Class A concrete?
questions.n: Class A concrete (1 part cement, 2 parts sand, 4 parts gravel) is the standard mix for beams, columns, and slabs.

questions.q: What is the purpose of "Rebars" in concrete?
o: To prevent the concrete from getting wet.
questions.n: Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension; steel rebars are added to 'pull' and handle the tensile loads.

questions.q: What is "Slump Test" used for on a construction site?
o: To check the final hardness of a cured slab.
To determine the weight of the steel rebars.
To test the soil bearing capacity before digging.
To measure the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.
questions.n: The slump test checks how much a concrete cone 'slumps' to ensure it has the correct water-to-cement ratio for pouring.

questions.q: What is the "Owner-Architect Agreement" document number?
questions.n: UAP Document 202 details the standard professional services, responsibilities, and fees between the architect and the owner.

questions.q: What is the "Architect's Credo"?
o: A list of the architect's project expenses.
A design philosophy for a specific building.
A formal statement of the architect's professional duties and ethics.
questions.n: The Credo serves as a moral compass, outlining the architect's commitment to the client, the public, and the profession.

questions.q: Who is the "Client" in a socialized condominium project?
o: The individual residents of the units.
Typically a Developer or a Government Agency (like NHA).
questions.n: Socialized housing is usually initiated by large developers for compliance or by agencies like the National Housing Authority.

questions.q: What is the percentage of the Architect's fee usually paid upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase?
questions.n: Standard UAP billing schedules allocate 15% of the total professional fee once the schematic design is approved.

questions.q: What is the "PRBOA"?
o: Public Registry of Building Operations and Architecture.
Professional Regional Building and Office Authority.
questions.n: The PRBOA is the government body under the PRC that regulates the practice of architecture in the Philippines.

questions.q: If the budget is very tight, what is the best window type to use for a socialized condo?
o: Jalousie Windows (for maximum ventilation and low cost).
questions.n: Jalousies are inexpensive, easy to repair, and provide 100% ventilation area, which is vital for non-AC units.

questions.q: To save space in a small studio unit, what type of door is best for a closet?
questions.n: Sliding doors do not require a 'swing' clearance, making them ideal for narrow rooms where every square inch of floor space counts.

questions.q: What is the most efficient water-saving fixture for a socialized housing project?
questions.n: Dual-flush systems allow users to choose a smaller water volume for liquid waste, significantly reducing overall building water consumption.

questions.q: What type of partition is best for dividing the living area and bedroom in a studio unit?
questions.n: Drywall partitions are lightweight, quick to install, and easily removable, providing flexibility without adding much weight to the slab.

questions.q: How do you address the "Heat Island Effect" on the roof of a condominium?
o: By removing all trees around the building.
By using high-reflectivity paint or a green roof.
questions.n: Reflective surfaces (cool roofs) or vegetation (green roofs) reduce the amount of solar heat absorbed and re-radiated by the building.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Grease Trap" in the kitchen sink of a unit?
o: To increase the water pressure in the sink.
To separate fats and oils from the wastewater.
questions.n: Grease traps intercept greasy waste before it enters the plumbing stack, preventing clogs and sewer backups.

questions.q: What is the best location for the "Service Area" (laundry) in a condo unit?
o: In the middle of the living room.
Adjacent to the kitchen or bathroom for easier plumbing access.
At the entrance of the unit.
questions.n: Grouping 'wet' areas together (wet blocks) reduces the length of pipe runs and simplifies the plumbing manifold design.

questions.q: What is the purpose of "Acoustic Sealant" in a condominium unit?
o: To make the paint look shiny.
To act as a structural adhesive for bricks.
To prevent sound from traveling through gaps in walls and ceilings.
To prevent water leaks in the bathroom.
questions.n: Even a high-STC wall fails if there are air gaps at the top or bottom; sealant blocks these paths for airborne noise.

questions.q: What is the standard height of a light switch from the floor?
questions.n: 1.20m is the standard ergonomic height for a standing adult to reach a switch without bending or reaching up.

questions.q: What is the standard height of a convenience outlet (C.O.) from the floor?
questions.n: Outlets are typically placed low at 0.30m to keep cords near the floor and maintain a clean wall aesthetic.
